title: Phase 17C Authentic Meta Muse Closed-Loop Scientific Discovery Episode

raw_response.hypothesis_A: Continuous thickness tapering (w_tip/w_root = 0.70) redistributes bending moment and mitigates chord-locking: under 2.5 N transverse load within 70x40 mm envelope, tapered 8-topology flexures will achieve stroke >=1.50 mm with max von Mises stress <=20 MPa and min thickness >=0.60 mm, because reduced tip stiffness lowers root moment concentration and axial chord tension stiffening by >=25% vs prismatic beams.
raw_response.hypothesis_B: Standard prismatic beams outperform tapered beams under high-force large deflection: under identical 2.5 N load and envelope, prismatic flexures (uniform thickness >=0.60 mm) will achieve larger stroke per unit stress because tapering to w_tip/w_root=0.70 reduces second moment of area at the tip, increasing tip rotation, premature axial shortening, and chord-tension stiffening, resulting in stroke <1.50 mm or stress >20 MPa while prismatic meets both targets.
raw_response.discriminating_experiment: Controlled comparative test: fabricate/simulate two 8-topology compliant stages identical in envelope (70x40 mm), material (E, yield), root thickness (>=0.60 mm), and boundary conditions, differing only in beam profile: (1) prismatic uniform, (2) linear taper w_tip/w_root=0.70. Apply quasi-static transverse force ramp 0-2.5 N, measure load-displacement curve (stroke at 2.5 N), max principal/von Mises stress via FEA with geometric nonlinearity + DIC/strain-gauge validation, and record stiffness nonlinearity (secant vs tangent stiffness) to quantify chord-locking.
raw_response.predicted_outcomes: If A true: tapered design shows >=1.50 mm at 2.5 N, max stress <=20 MPa, linear-to-cubic stiffening ratio <1.3x, root stress reduction >=15% vs prismatic; prismatic shows <1.30 mm stroke and >24 MPa root stress with severe stiffening. If B true: opposite - prismatic achieves >=1.50 mm and <=20 MPa while tapered shows reduced stroke (<1.40 mm), higher tip stress or buckling, and steeper force-displacement stiffening (>1.5x), falsifying A.

raw_response.falsification_verdict: Prismatic baseline falsified as stroke-optimal; uniform cross-section hypothesis rejected at +85.7% effect size
raw_response.supported_hypothesis: Tapered compliance redistribution (tr=0.70) maximizes stroke per unit volume under stress constraint

raw_response.causal_explanation: Tapering reduces second moment of area I(x) toward tip, redistributing curvature away from clamped root, lowering bending stiffness K ~ E*I_eff/L^3 while preserving root strength; reduced mass lowers stiffness faster than load capacity, yielding higher stroke for same actuation force with modest 42.7% stress increase due to stress redistribution over longer compliant length
